news.headline: DaVita Inc. Stock
news.quote: DaVita Expands Availability Of Expanded Hemodialysis Therapy To Every U.S. Center

touches.claim: The company says it is an industry leader on CMS quality measures, which supports its clinical reputation with patients and payors.

Treatment volume is a small and fragile contributor: normalized non-acquired treatment growth was 0.4% in the third quarter, driven by patient census increases. For this to continue, mortality, flu impact and missed treatments must not worsen and admissions must hold.

news.why: DaVita expanded availability of expanded hemodialysis therapy across all of its U.S. centers, modestly supporting its clinical quality positioning and patient treatment retention.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A (P3) and described in the 10-K Business section (P1)
business_model.claim: DaVita's core business is selling dialysis and related lab services to patients with chronic kidney failure (ESKD), mainly in the United States.
quotes: Our principal business is to provide dialysis and related lab services to patients in the United States, which we refer to as our U.S. dialysis business.

business_model.claim: U.S. dialysis is the dominant revenue source, at about 86% of 2025 consolidated revenues.
quotes: Approximately 86% of our 2025 consolidated revenues were derived directly from our U.S. dialysis business.

business_model.basis: stated in P3; the segment table in P6 uses the same split
business_model.claim: The company reports a U.S. dialysis business, ancillary services (U.S. integrated kidney care, other U.S. ancillary and international), and a corporate administrative support function.
quotes: We also operate our U.S. integrated kidney care (IKC) business, our U.S. other ancillary services, and our international operations, which we collectively refer to as our ancillary services, as well as our corporate administrative support functions.

business_model.basis: stated in the P6 supplemental tables; the comparison across segments is inferred
business_model.claim: In Q3 2026, U.S. dialysis produced revenue of $3,050 and segment operating income of $544 (table in millions). Consolidated revenue was $3,578 and operating income was $499. The ancillary services combined result was (19) and corporate administrative support expenses were (26), so U.S. dialysis carries the group's profit.
Scale at September 30, 2026: about 298,100 patients served at 3,269 outpatient dialysis centers, of which 2,671 are in the U.S. and 598 are in 14 other countries.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we provided dialysis services to a total of approximately 298,100 patients at 3,269 outpatient dialysis centers, of which 2,671 centers were located in the United States and 598 centers were located in 14 countries outside of the United States.

business_model.claim: U.S. dialysis revenue comes from three settings: outpatient centers, home-based dialysis and hospital inpatient services.
quotes: Our outpatient, home-based and hospital inpatient dialysis services comprise approximately 76%, 18% and 6% of our U.S. dialysis revenues, respectively.

business_model.claim: Most U.S. dialysis revenue and most patients are government-paid, led by Medicare and Medicare Advantage. Commercial payors account for about 32% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenues.
quotes: For 2025, approximately 68% of our total U.S. dialysis patient service revenues were generated from government-based programs for services to approximately 89% of our total U.S. patients.
Commercial payors (including hospital dialysis services) represent approximately 32% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenues.

business_model.basis: stated in the risk factor (P2); the higher-rate comparison is stated in P3
business_model.claim: Commercial insurance is the profit engine. Commercial rates are significantly higher than government rates, and the company says commercial payments generate nearly all of its profit.
quotes: The payments we receive from commercial payors generate nearly all of our profit and all of our nonacute dialysis profits come from commercial payors.

business_model.basis: drivers stated in P3; Q3 figures stated in P6
business_model.claim: U.S. dialysis revenue is driven by treatment volume and by average patient service revenue per treatment, including the payor mix. In Q3 2026 there were 7,329,644 treatments at $415.25 per treatment, and normalized non-acquired treatment growth was 0.4%.
quotes: our average dialysis patient service revenue per treatment, including the mix of patients with commercial plans and government programs as primary payor.
Normalized non-acquired treatment growth in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025 was 0.4%.

business_model.claim: Year-to-date revenue per treatment rose to $416.22 from $405.15, helped by annual rate increases and held back by an unfavorable payor mix.
quotes: The year to date change was driven by typical annual rate increases and other normal fluctuations, partially offset by unfavorable changes in payor mix.

business_model.claim: Medicare sets much of the pricing. CMS finalized a 2.2% average reimbursement increase for freestanding ESRD facilities in 2026, and phosphate binders are paid through a temporary add-on (TDAPA) period set to expire at the end of 2026.
quotes: CMS has finalized ESRD freestanding facilities' average reimbursement by an increase of 2.2% in 2026.

business_model.basis: stated in F2; the identification of the largest expense is inferred from the table

business_model.basis: cost drivers stated in P3; per-treatment figures stated in P6
business_model.claim: Patient care costs depend on labor, drug and supply pricing and use, and center infrastructure. U.S. dialysis patient care costs per treatment were $280.22 in Q3 2026 versus $277.40 in Q2, and $279.24 year to date versus $271.23.
quotes: labor costs, including clinical hours per treatment, labor rates and benefit costs;
The year to date change was primarily driven by increased compensation expenses, medical supplies expense, insurance costs and health benefits expenses.

business_model.claim: The integrated kidney care (IKC) business is paid through value-based and risk-based arrangements. At September 30, 2026 it covered about 80,800 patients in risk-based arrangements, representing about $6.4 billion of annualized medical spend. It reported Q3 revenue of 144 (table in millions).
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we had approximately 80,800 patients in risk-based integrated care arrangements representing approximately $6.4 billion in annualized medical spend.

Our IKC business also utilizes other value-based payment methodologies in its care coordination and disease management contracts, which include two-sided shared savings/shared losses and outcomes-based pay-for-performance compensation arrangements.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited items for the rate-increase driver. The condition on payor mix is inferred from the 10-K profit concentration statement.
growth_thesis.claim: U.S. dialysis pricing is a growth driver: dialysis patient service revenues were 3,408,266 (table in thousands) in the third quarter against 3,298,090 a year earlier, and nine-month revenue per treatment was $416.22 against $405.15. The company attributes the year-to-date change to annual rate increases. For this to continue, annual rate increases must keep coming and payor mix must stop deteriorating.

The payments we receive from commercial payors generate nearly all of our profit and all of our nonacute dialysis profits come from commercial payors.

growth_thesis.claim: Treatment volume is a small and fragile contributor: normalized non-acquired treatment growth was 0.4% in the third quarter, driven by patient census increases. For this to continue, mortality, flu impact and missed treatments must not worsen and admissions must hold.

In the third quarter of 2026, treatment per day volumes increased compared to the third quarter of 2025 primarily driven by patient census increases that were partially offset by a slight increase in missed treatment rates.
In 2026 in our U.S. dialysis business, we expect approximately flat treatment volumes due to the net impact of a number of factors.
